references.text: Both texts deal with how innocent bloodshed defiles the land that the Lord has given to Israel.
Concerns legislation on murder and the need for witnesses to determine guilt.
Legislation regarding responsibility when someone is killed without the murderer being known.
Deals with cities of refuge for those who have killed someone accidentally, related to unknown murder guilt.
Parallel legislation on murder, bloodguilt, and cities of refuge in the land the Lord gives to Israel.
Emphasizes the importance of avoiding innocent bloodshed in the land the Lord gives as an inheritance.
Cain's blood cries out from the ground - an early example of bloodguilt affecting the earth.
